path_placeholders.@WORKSPACE@: the scenario workspace the probe treats as the only writable directory
path_placeholders.@BASE@: the workspace's parent, holding the read, write and delete canaries outside the boundary
path_placeholders.@NODE_TREE@: the install prefix of the node binary that runs the probes
path_placeholders.@RUNTIME_CLI_TREE@: the install prefix of the agent CLIs
path_placeholders.@AGENT_TEMP_HOME@: the temporary HOME a BEST_EFFORT_CLI run creates
path_placeholders.@HOSTNAME@: the probing machine's network name, removed from recorded output

properties.question: Can the agent read a file inside the scenario workspace?
Can the agent write a file inside the scenario workspace?
Can the agent read a file in the workspace's parent directory?
Can the agent create a file outside the workspace?
Can the agent delete a file outside the workspace that already existed?
Can the agent list the operator's real home by absolute path, ignoring $HOME?
Can the agent read bytes of a private key under the operator's ~/.ssh by absolute path?
Can the agent read the runtime's own credential file under the operator's home?
Can the agent read AOS_HOME -- run records, results, holdout ledger -- by absolute path?
Can the agent read outside the workspace through a symlink planted inside it?
Can the agent start a child process at all?
Can a process the agent spawned read outside the boundary?
Can the agent leave a detached process running after AOS tears the run down?
Can such a survivor still read outside the boundary once it has been orphaned?
Can the agent open an outbound TCP connection?
Can the agent retrieve the value of an item in the operator's login keychain?

backends.mechanism: sandbox-exec(1) with a (deny default) Seatbelt profile allowing only the system tree, the probe files read-only, and the workspace
limitations: sandbox-exec(1) is documented DEPRECATED in its own man page on macOS 26.3 and still enforces. Apple can withdraw it with no deprecation period left to spend.
The profile names no runtime install tree, so no agent CLI can be exec'd under it. Its authentication cells measure exec and say nothing about credentials.
sandbox-exec's own failure codes -- 65 for a missing or invalid profile, 71 when it cannot exec -- collide with ordinary runtime exit codes, which was measured directly.
/bin/ps cannot be exec'd inside any profile on this machine, including (allow default), because it is setgid. Anything inside the boundary that needs to enumerate processes has to do it another way.

observations.note: Denied, and this profile is the reason: it deliberately does not name the keychain. AOS resolves the Claude Code credential in the parent and injects it into the child environment (lib/runtime-auth.mjs), so a confined child does not need keychain access to authenticate.

backends.mechanism: The deny-default profile plus named read-only holes for the runtime's credential directory and install tree, and outbound network for the provider transport. The login keychain is deliberately not named
limitations: The process axis is open. A detached descendant takes its own session, escapes the process group AOS signals, and is not listed by lib/core.mjs processGroupMembers -- measured against that function directly.

`authenticated_runtime` is true on the strength of the Codex cell. The Claude Code cell under this profile is not logged in, because nothing here supplies its credential; AOS's own resolver would, and that path was not exercised.
Deprecated interface, as the deny-default row.
Network is allowed wholesale. Provider transport and task-initiated external calls are not distinguishable at this layer, so a claim resting on that distinction has to be recorded NOT_OBSERVED.

backends.mechanism: OCI container on the Linux VM reachable from this darwin host (Docker 29.4.0 server, OrbStack kernel 7.0.11, linux/arm64), workspace bind-mounted, --network none
limitations: Every measured boundary row holds and the teardown reaps the descendant. What fails is the runtime: the operator's installed codex carries only @openai/codex-darwin-arm64 and refused to start, which was measured rather than inferred.
`boundary_canary: PASS` covers the fifteen properties that were observed here. The orphan row is not_observed, because no orphan survived to test.
Running an agent here means the container carries its own Linux install of the CLI and its own copy of the credential -- live credential material inside the namespace the assessed agent writes to.
The Linux kernel reached from this host is a VM. A result produced here describes the VM, not the operator's macOS machine.
A macOS keychain credential cannot be delivered into a Linux namespace at all.

authentication_cells.note: The control every other cell is read against.

authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && claude auth status   # stdout reduced to loggedIn and authMethod before recording
authentication_cells.note: Reduced to loggedIn and authMethod before recording; the command also prints the operator's account.

authentication_cells.description: The environment AOS builds today: buildAgentEnv("BEST_EFFORT_CLI", process.env, { home: <temp> }).
authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && <env from buildAgentEnv("BEST_EFFORT_CLI", process.env, { home: <temp> })> codex login status
authentication_cells.note: CODEX_HOME is in the adapter's allow list (lib/profile.mjs config_env, carried by the discovered agent at lib/cli.mjs) but was not set in the operator's environment on this machine, so nothing was there to carry and ~/.codex moved with HOME.

authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && <env from buildAgentEnv("BEST_EFFORT_CLI", process.env, { home: <temp> })> claude auth status   # stdout reduced to loggedIn and authMethod before recording
authentication_cells.note: The login keychain is resolved from HOME. This cell does not exercise AOS's own resolver, which reads the keychain in the parent and injects CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.

authentication_cells.description: The same environment, with CODEX_HOME carried and pointed at the real config directory.
authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && CODEX_HOME=@OPERATOR_HOME@/.codex CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=@OPERATOR_HOME@/.claude <env from buildAgentEnv with allow:[CODEX_HOME,CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR]> codex login status
authentication_cells.note: This is the cell that isolates the cause. HOME replacement alone loses the credential; HOME replacement with the adapter's config directory carried keeps it. #555 measured the same thing independently and has since made config_env part of the allow list.

authentication_cells.description: The same, with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR carried and pointed at ~/.claude.
authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && CODEX_HOME=@OPERATOR_HOME@/.codex CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=@OPERATOR_HOME@/.claude <env from buildAgentEnv with allow:[CODEX_HOME,CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR]> claude auth status   # stdout reduced to loggedIn and authMethod before recording
authentication_cells.note: A config directory does not carry this runtime's credential on macOS -- the adapter says so itself -- so carrying it changes nothing. What would restore this cell is AOS's keychain resolver, which was not exercised here.

authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && sandbox-exec -f deny-default.sb codex login status
authentication_cells.note: This cell measures exec, not authentication: the profile does not name the runtime's install tree, so sandbox-exec refused to exec the binary at all. It is recorded because an earlier draft read this exit as an authentication failure.

authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && sandbox-exec -f deny-default.sb claude auth status   # stdout reduced to loggedIn and authMethod before recording
authentication_cells.note: Same exec refusal as the codex cell above.

authentication_cells.description: Confined, with the credential directory, the install tree and outbound network named.
authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && sandbox-exec -f provider-lane.sb codex login status
authentication_cells.note: The result that matters: real confinement and a real login at the same time, with the operator's own HOME and the filesystem refused by the kernel.

authentication_cells.description: The same profile, which does not name the keychain.
authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && sandbox-exec -f provider-lane.sb claude auth status   # stdout reduced to loggedIn and authMethod before recording
authentication_cells.note: Expected, and not a verdict on the runtime: nothing in this profile or this cell supplies the credential. AOS's resolver would inject it from the parent, and that path was not exercised.

authentication_cells.description: The provider lane with the login keychain additionally granted.
authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && sandbox-exec -f keychain-lane.sb codex login status

authentication_cells.description: The provider lane with the login keychain additionally granted.
authentication_cells.command: cd @WORKSPACE@ && sandbox-exec -f keychain-lane.sb claude auth status   # stdout reduced to loggedIn and authMethod before recording
authentication_cells.note: The keychain grant is what this runtime's authentication needed inside the boundary. It is measured to show what the grant buys, not to propose it: the same result should be reachable from the parent's resolver without opening the keychain to the child at all.

authentication_cells.description: The operator's installed CLI, bind-mounted into a Linux container.
authentication_cells.command: docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 --network none -v @OPERATOR_HOME@/.local/lib/node_modules/@openai/codex:/codex:ro node:22-bookworm node /codex/bin/codex.js login status
authentication_cells.note: This cell measures execution, not authentication. The install carries only the darwin-arm64 binary.
